_readme: The Little Fortune Shop: every fortune the jar can give.
signature: hand-written fortunes. Rare and Very Rare fortunes always come from here.
phrases: building blocks. The jar combines them into thousands of fortunes:
A = subject + predicate + when      B = action + ", and " + result      C = image + meaning
To add fortunes: add lines to the END of any list. Do not reorder or delete existing lines,
because saved journals remember fortunes by their position in these lists.

luck.text: Somewhere, a door is already opening for you.
The coin you dropped long ago is still rolling toward something good.
Luck rarely knocks. It usually just leaves the window open.
The bus you missed was never yours. The next one knows your name.
A small yes is on its way, hidden inside an ordinary afternoon.
Today, the odds are leaning quietly in your direction.
Something you misplaced will turn up exactly when you stop looking.
The umbrella you nearly forgot will matter more than you think.
A lucky thing is easiest to see from a slower pace.
Keep a pocket empty this week. Something wants to fill it.
Good fortune prefers people who leave room for it.
The rain is not against you. It is watering what you planted.
A stranger will hand you something, and it will not be by accident.
Three small coincidences are a pattern. Follow the third one.
What you call a near miss, the year will later call a turning point.
You are luckier than your worries have been telling you.
Some fortunes take seven days to arrive. Yours has already set out.
The cat at the counter has decided you are good luck. It is rarely wrong.
The thing you wished for once and forgot about has not forgotten you.
Few hands reach this paper. The shop has been saving it for you.

friendship.text: Someone is thinking of you right now and smiling at the memory.
A friendship is a lantern two people agree to keep lit.
The friend who arrives late usually stays the longest.
You are someone’s favorite person to tell good news to.
Old friends are like old teacups: a little chipped, entirely irreplaceable.
Send the message you have been drafting in your head.
Somebody remembers a kindness you have long forgotten.
Good company can turn any bench into a fine place to be.
The quiet friend has been paying more attention than anyone.
A shared umbrella is worth more than a dry walk alone.
Laughter that comes easily is a sign you are among your people.
A friend you have not met yet already likes the same strange things you do.
Distance is just the space a friendship stretches into. It does not tear.
Someone will soon need exactly the thing you are good at.
Friendships are not measured in hours, but in how easily the silence sits.
You have been somebody’s shelter more often than you know.
An old thread between you and someone far away is about to be pulled gently.
Bring two cups next time. Someone is on their way.
The people who stay through the ordinary days are the rarest of all.
Long ago, someone wished they would meet a person like you. It worked.

love.text: Love often arrives disguised as a very ordinary conversation.
Be as gentle with yourself as you are with the people you love.
The heart keeps a better calendar than the mind.
Somewhere, a song reminds someone of you.
Small attentions, repeated, become a kind of devotion.
Love does not need to shout. It is happy to simply stay.
What you give freely has a way of finding its way home.
Warm tea, a kind word, a hand held a moment longer. That is enough.
Be open to the person who makes you laugh at the wrong moment.
The right person will think your quiet parts are the best parts.
There is someone who would walk through the rain just to hear your news.
A love worth keeping makes you more like yourself, not less.
The thing you are most afraid to say is the thing they hope to hear.
A letter you never sent still did its work on you.
Your heart has been mending in the background, like a kettle slowly warming.
You will be loved for the very thing you once tried to hide.
Two umbrellas will soon become one. Do not be surprised.
The longest love stories begin with someone noticing a small detail.
Somebody kept something you gave them, and they look at it often.
The red thread is real. It is shorter than you think.

courage.text: Not every detour takes you farther from where you belong.
Brave does not mean unafraid. It means you went anyway.
The first step is usually smaller than the one you are imagining.
Your voice is steadier than it sounds from the inside.
Courage can be as quiet as getting up again tomorrow.
You have survived every one of your hardest days so far.
A closed door is still a door. Knock once more.
Say the true thing kindly, and let it land where it may.
Fear is a lantern held too close. Step back and it becomes light.
The road looks steepest from the bottom. Look again from halfway.
Let yourself be a beginner at something. It is a gentle kind of bravery.
The mountain does not mind how slowly you climb it.
Someone is watching you try, and it is giving them courage too.
You are allowed to change your mind and walk a different path.
Storms pass over roofs that hold. Yours is holding.
The tremble in your hands is just the sound of something mattering.
The version of you from five years ago would be astonished by today.
A small, brave act this week will echo further than you expect.
The bamboo bends in the storm and is still standing at sunrise.
You were made for at least one moment that requires exactly this courage.

creativity.text: The smallest beginnings often carry the longest stories.
Make something badly first. Beauty arrives on the second try.
Your odd idea is the one worth keeping.
A blank page is just a quiet room waiting for a guest.
Inspiration enjoys a slow walk. Take it somewhere new.
Copy the masters once, then make the mistake that is only yours.
Keep a notebook nearby. Tonight’s dream wants to be written down.
Your hands know things your mind has not figured out yet.
A little boredom is the soil where ideas grow.
Finish the small thing. It will teach you how to finish the big one.
Steal a color from the evening sky. No one will mind.
The thing you made and set aside deserves a second look.
The best ideas arrive while you are doing the dishes. Let them.
You do not need permission to make something beautiful.
Somewhere, a stranger will be comforted by something you create.
Rain on a window is a kind of music. Listen for the melody.
What you are building slowly is going to outlast what others build quickly.
An unfinished sketch of yours holds the start of something remarkable.
Make the thing you wished existed. Someone else has been wishing too.
A small piece of your imagination is going to travel very far.

beginnings.text: Every morning is a page that has never been written on.
You do not need a new year to begin again. A Tuesday will do.
Plant the seed even if you will not see the tree.
The first cup of tea is always the most honest.
A fresh start can be as simple as opening a window.
Something is ending so that something kinder can arrive.
Begin where you are. It is the only place anyone ever begins.
A new chapter does not erase the old ones. It builds on them.
Pack lightly. The new road will give you what you need.
The blossoms do not apologize for arriving late in the spring.
Change usually arrives quietly, while you are looking the other way.
The path ahead is unfamiliar because it is yours, not someone else’s.
A small decision this month will turn out to be the first step of a long journey.
You are allowed to outgrow places that once fit you perfectly.
The key to the next door is already in your pocket.
Every ending is a hallway, and hallways lead to rooms.
The season you are entering will feel like coming home to yourself.
Someone you will meet this year is going to change your direction for the better.
The tide is turning. You will notice it first in small things.
This is the beginning you will tell stories about one day.

wisdom.text: You may find what you need in a place you almost overlooked.
Steep slowly. The best flavors take their time.
Not every question needs an answer today.
The river does not push. It simply keeps going.
When in doubt, drink some water and go to bed early.
Listen twice as long as you speak, and you will hear what is unsaid.
Patience is just hope that has learned to sit down.
A cluttered mind is like a cloudy pot of tea. Let it settle.
Sometimes the kindest answer is a good question.
The moon does not compete with the lanterns. It simply shines.
You already know the answer. You are only waiting to be sure.
The things that worry you at night are smaller in the morning light.
A crack in the bowl is where the gold goes.
Rest is not the opposite of progress. It is part of it.
What is meant for you will not need to be chased.
Even a slow walk eventually reaches the top of the hill.
The teacup is useful because it is empty. Make a little space.
You have learned more this year than any book could have taught you.
The mountain is not in a hurry, and still it reaches the clouds.
Whatever you are carrying, you are allowed to set it down for a while.

surprises.text: A pleasant surprise is hiding in an ordinary week.
Check your coat pockets. Something small and good is waiting.
A song you have not heard in years will find you soon.
The next envelope you open will make you smile.
Something you thought was lost is only taking the long way home.
An unexpected guest will bring exactly the right conversation.
Look up tonight. The sky has arranged something for you.
A detour on your usual walk will reveal a hidden garden.
You will taste something new and wonder where it has been all your life.
A small kindness from a stranger will brighten a gray day.
Somebody is about to say something that changes your mind entirely.
The rain will stop at precisely the right moment.
A dusty box holds something you will be glad to have kept.
Your name will be mentioned somewhere good, and you may never know it.
The thing you dread on the calendar will turn out to be the highlight.
A door you walk past every day is worth opening once.
An old wish is folding itself into something better than you asked for.
The fortune you were meant to get was this one. The jar insisted.
A small mystery will be solved, and the answer will be lovely.
Tonight the shopkeeper left a lantern burning just for you. Look closely.

images: The tea leaves settle when no one is watching.
Rain does not hurry, yet it fills every river.
The moon is never late, only patient.
A kettle sings only once the water is ready.
Plum blossoms open in the cold before anyone expects them.
The river carves stone without ever raising its voice.
Lanterns are lit one at a time.
Snow melts from the edges first.
A single cup of tea can warm both hands.
Bamboo grows roots for years before it rises.
The tide goes out so that it can come back in.
Moss grows best where it is left alone.
A paper crane begins as a single fold.
Even the longest rain ends in a puddle full of sky.
The cat sleeps in whatever patch of sun it finds.
Seeds do not argue with the season.
Morning fog lifts without being asked.
An old teapot pours best after years of use.
The stars were there all day; it simply took the dark to see them.
The heron waits so long that the river forgets it is there.
